title: BBC Learning English from the News 2026 — Quiz 10
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q091_wounded
elements.title: Several players were ___ by flying glass when a window broke.

elements.name: q092_open_fire
elements.title: Which expression means “start shooting” in a novel or a news report?

elements.name: q093_chilling
elements.title: The witness gave a ___ account that left listeners deeply frightened.

elements.name: q094_swept_away
elements.title: The current ___ the floating dock and carried it downstream.

elements.name: q095_brick_by_brick
elements.title: The volunteers rebuilt the organisation ___, solving one small problem at a time.

elements.name: q096_kindred_spirit
elements.title: They quickly bonded over the same unusual interests. Each had found a ___.

elements.name: q097_a_new_dawn
elements.title: The reopening marked ___ for the neighbourhood, as long-empty shops began to fill again.

elements.name: q098_lose_contact_with
elements.title: After changing numbers and moving abroad, he began to ___ old friends he used to speak to weekly.

elements.name: q099_a_big_deal
elements.title: “Getting that scholarship is a big deal for Mina.” What does the speaker mean?
choices: She is planning to turn it down.
She must pay a large fee for it.
It is an ordinary part of her routine.
It is very important to her.
elements.correctAnswer: It is very important to her.

elements.name: q100_having_a_moment
elements.title: “She’s having a moment after hearing the news. Give her a minute.” What does the phrase suggest here?
choices: She is waiting for an appointment.
She is feeling strong emotions for a short time.
elements.correctAnswer: She is feeling strong emotions for a short time.
